_about: Owner's direction, Sept 21, 2026: make the learn-research-trade-fail-or-succeed loop as rapid as possible and use every input. Applied on top of the funded burst policy (whose record and spend caps are unchanged). Measured before: Luna sessions median 12 s, Sail pro_flex 241 s (p90 1,178 s); Sail was the underused budget. 20:26 UTC: all 16 research workers were busy with Sail sessions (multi-turn, replays inside), so 24. 22:10 UTC, owner adds $200 OpenAI and $100 Sail and asks for more gas: research every 5 min (winners every ~1.7), 32/8 workers, a newcomer every 2 min, population 64, Luna (median 12 s) back to three quarters. 23:55 UTC: rung-0 agents, which write all new code, averaged 8 research sessions in four hours on a $2 endowment and were displaced (median life 4.3 h); the endowment is 8. Sept 22, 2026 (overnight rebuild): Merton's burst cadence is re-allocated by measured yield (merton_schedule_hours). Lifetime to Sept 22: the operator ran 54 passes and nearly always left the dials unchanged (its one merge was harmful), the designer ran 16 and never changed game.json, the toolsmith's 8 PRs were all refused by CI, the architect landed 4 strategies from 6 PRs, the teacher merged 13 of 13. At burst cadence the first three cost about $5 an hour at campaign prices; that attention now goes to the hypothesis foundry and the repair engineer, which have their own caps. Role backoff on empty passes still applies. Sept 23, 2026 (owner: 'do 1-5 right now fully'): research every 15 minutes with 16 workers (84% of sessions abstained, most by agents with no record; the unproven wait three intervals), and 12 replay workers, because the foundry's cards now queue for replay beside every agent's own. Sept 23, 2026, later (owner: 'address all the largest gaps'): population 96, because the foundry's cards passed replay about half the time while three waited for seats in a league capped at 64 and research is now paced by record, so a seat costs little; and Merton's scheduled roles by measured yield again -- operator every 48 h, designer 96 h (almost never changed anything), toolsmith and architect 12 h (the Sol foundry now writes strategies at about a sixth of an Astra architect pass), teacher 4 h -- because their rounds after 01:39Z cost $2.41 and $2.29 of a September OpenAI line with $91 left at 02:50Z (the gateway measured $5.1 an hour since 23:50Z). And research moves to Luna (0.95 of agents; 0.05 stays on Sail as the comparison): measured 01:39-02:10Z Sept 23, a Sail pro_asap session cost about $0.06 and a Luna one about $0.011 (a valid strategy $0.011 on Luna against $0.12-0.22 on DeepSeek, Sept 22), and Sail research was most of the ~$35 a day that leaves about three days of Sail credit, while the OpenAI month resets on Oct 1. Sept 23, 2026, 04:35 UTC: fork_threshold_usd 10, above the $8 endowment, so a newborn forks only once it has earned credits; at the burst's $2, 22 parameter copies were forked in the 40 minutes after the swing-and-bunt deploy and filled the desks the foundry's replay-passing cards waited for (the foundry refused every call from 04:01Z). Sept 23, 2026, 16:41 UTC (the learn-and-unblock run, C3 pacing): the September OpenAI line had $34.92 left at 16:21Z and burned about $5 an hour; paced to the House line over the hours left (about $3.30 an hour) so the month keeps its $8 audit floor at the deadline. The toolsmith (8 PRs, all refused by CI, $17.72 this month) waits 48 h and the architect (4 strategies from 6 PRs, $47.30 this month; the GPT-6 Sol foundry writes strategies at about a sixth of an architect pass) 24 h; the teacher (13 of 13 merged) keeps 4 h and audits keep their tier. Re-read hourly against the burn. Sept 23, 2026, 19:00 UTC (the learn-and-unblock run, the seat market follows evidence): population 96 -> 112 and a newcomer every 600 s, not 120. The House's own parameter mutations were 327 of 441 births and 274 of 312 displacements (median life 3.8 h, 24% ever passed replay) while 20 lab graduates, 6 replay-passed cards and 6 merged strategies waited for seats; now no mutation is staked while any of them waits, and one at most every ten minutes otherwise. Sail: the balance was $96 at $32 a day (3.0 days), of which box time was about $2.6 a day for 96 boxes ($0.027 a box a day), so 16 more boxes cost about $0.43 a day: 2.9 days of runway, above the 1.5-day floor the plan keeps. Sept 23, 2026, 23:10 UTC (the learn-and-unblock run, the Sail floor): once the OpenAI month fell to the "earned" tier (about 20:50Z) cheap-model research moved to Sail, and with 112 agents researching on evidence triggers Sail spend rose from $0.6-1.8 an hour (17-20Z) to $5.8 (20-22Z) and $11.66 (22-23Z, 344 calls): the $76 balance would last about six hours against the plan's floor of 1.5 days of runway. Research is growth, and the plan stops growth before anything that trades: the base research interval is 120 minutes (winners every 12 minutes, unproven agents every 12 hours, losers every 16 hours) and 6 workers, until Sail is recharged or the OpenAI month resets on Oct 1. A refused order still gets its prompt research, and every agent keeps trading its deployed program.
